checklist.fact: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, for MoDOT as the beneficiary (Right of Way staff are the users of the tool).
The need: property descriptions for MHTC must be written by metes and bounds and reviewed by a professional land surveyor, and these descriptions are long and tedious to write.
The project goal is to determine the usefulness of AI and ML to develop a "first draft" legal land description using MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would review and edit.
The services are capped at a not-to-exceed price of $175,000.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project assumed to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending February 2, 2026 with the final invoice due.
Proposals for project TR202504 must be emailed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
Questions must be submitted by 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central via the RFP email only; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification.
Property descriptions must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, which the RFP references but does not include.

Core deliverables include a data management plan, a proof-of-concept demonstration of AI writing legal land descriptions, training and a user manual for ROW staff, and draft and final reports; the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.
Web applications must meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility conformance.
No PII may be stored in any database table unless there is a specific business need, and any stored PII requires approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and reporting
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the study against a work plan and schedule that MoDOT approves, with the kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024 to confirm scope, schedule and a communications protocol, and minutes issued for the kick-off and every quarterly status meeting. Quarterly status meetings review the prior period and the next, quarterly written updates go electronically to the MoDOT project manager by the last working day of March, June, September and December so they feed the SPR Quarterly Report, and monthly email and phone contact keeps MoDOT current between meetings. The component also carries the interim presentation at the project mid-point (9/15/2025) and the final presentation to MoDOT staff, and it holds the 15-month contract period, the 2/2/2026 final invoice date and the $175,000 ceiling as tracked baselines with earned-value style burn reporting.

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML practice
component_records.description: A structured search and review of how other state DOTs use AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, agency guidance and vendor practice, delivered as a written review with an annotated source list and a synthesis of what is transferable to MoDOT's LLD drafting problem. The review is completed early in the schedule so its findings shape the program design and the proof-of-concept property selection rather than trailing them, and it is carried forward into the draft and final reports.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and non-proprietary data handling
component_records.description: A Data Management Plan submitted within two weeks of the kick-off (12/4/2024) that specifies the data the study will use, how parcel and deed information is stored and secured, retention and disposition, and the platform-independent, non-proprietary formats (open text, CSV, PDF/A, plain source code) in which data and outputs will be delivered so MoDOT retains maximum future utility. The plan also states that no PII is stored in any database table without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval, and it governs how MHTC-supplied information is handled throughout.

component_records.title: LLD drafting program: design, technology approval and build
component_records.description: The Offeror designs and builds the program that generates first-draft legal land descriptions from MHTC parameters, and names that program to MoDOT before any proof-of-concept work begins so MoDOT Information Systems can approve it. The build is web-based on .NET 6.0 or above with MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, written in C#, JavaScript, CSS and HTML, with Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Best Practices Review Team approves more; it requires only a modern browser, carries no third-party component that would place a licensing obligation on MoDOT without prior BRPT and IS management approval, and displays no vendor branding where it can be removed. Where an on-premise database is used it runs on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server, and the application meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard.

component_records.title: Proof of concept on a variety of properties
component_records.description: A demonstration, delivered by 4/25/2025, in which the program produces draft legal land descriptions for a spread of property types — full-take parcels, partial takes requiring metes-and-bounds descriptions, and properties conveyed in their entirety where the description must match the last deed of record exactly. Each draft is checked against MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 and reviewed by a professional land surveyor before it is presented, and MoDOT Right of Way staff review the drafts and return structured improvement feedback that drives a documented revision cycle. The component includes the adjustment period after the demonstration that feeds the training and manual deliverable.

component_records.title: Training and user manual for Right of Way staff
component_records.description: A user manual and a delivered training package for MoDOT Right of Way staff, completed by 7/25/2025 after the tool adjustments from the proof-of-concept feedback. The manual covers parameter entry, generating and editing a draft description, the surveyor review step and the EPG 236.4.6.2 checks, and the training is delivered in a format and session count sized to the ROW audience with recorded sessions and quick-reference material left behind so new staff can be onboarded without the Offeror. The manual is reissued with the draft deliverables on 11/3/2025 and the final deliverables on 1/1/2026 so it stays current with the final tool.

component_records.title: Reports, research summary and final presentation
component_records.description: A draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with accompanying documentation (11/3/2025), then a final report detailing every task and all findings with a completed Technical Report Documentation page, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff (1/1/2026). All deliverables follow MoDOT's Publication Guidelines and research summary template and are supplied in the non-proprietary formats set out in the Data Management Plan.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and client-administration obligations
component_records.description: A compliance lead owns the contractual surface of the engagement: the signed Price Page cost estimate broken out by salaries, benefits, operating expense, F&A and miscellaneous with a total, and the commitment to perform at the quoted fees within the $175,000 ceiling. The component covers the E-Verify enrollment affidavit with its Memorandum of Understanding, the sworn affidavit that no unauthorized alien is knowingly employed, and Exhibit B lawful-presence affidavits where the entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership; it also carries the insurance certificates for general liability, automobile liability and Missouri workers' compensation if requested before signing. It administers MHTC ownership of all documents and MHTC-supplied information, the no-public-release rule, the no-assignment rule, the flow-down of Section (3) paragraph I into every subcontract, confidentiality and immediate notice of any third-party request for confidential information, and three-year record availability to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor after final payment, with all concerns routed to MHTC's designated representative and coordination maintained with the Construction and Materials Division.

pairs.requirement_text: The contract period will run for 15 months.
Quarterly updates on work accomplished must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December during the project.
An interim presentation must be scheduled near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and direction.
Monthly e-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts are required to provide ongoing updates of progress.
A kick-off meeting with MoDOT must be scheduled for 11/15/2024 to discuss project requirements and deliverables.
The interim presentation must be completed by 9/15/2025.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends 2/2/2026.
The services provided by the successful Offeror must not exceed $175,000.
The Offeror must facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and establish a protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination.
The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings to review progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next period.
The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and each quarterly status meeting.
The Offeror must provide a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing important or significant details of the project.

The Offeror must fully coordinate its activities for MHTC with those of the Construction and Materials Division and make advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division throughout the effective period.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for ROW purposes.
The data management plan is due 12/4/2024.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within 2 weeks after the project kick-off meeting.
The Data Management Plan should address how the Offeror will use platform-independent and non-proprietary formats to ensure maximum future utility of the data.
No Personal Identifiable Information may be stored in any database table unless the application has a specific business need, and all stored PII must be approved by the IS Cyber Security Team.
Before work begins on the proof of concept, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the LLDs.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the program before the Offeror may move forward with Task 3c.
All applications must be developed using one of the approved technologies listed in the RFP, such as .NET 6.0 or above (or .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed).
Web applications must use either the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework.

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team and IS management.

New development should use the approved programming languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and other small one-time uses unless large-scale use is approved by the IS Best Practices Review Team.
All customer applications should be web-based browser applications tested and designed to use the latest IS approved browser(s) at a minimum.
No client-side software other than a modern browser (for example, no Java Applets or Silverlight) should be required to run the web application.

On-premise database deployments must run on Oracle 19C or on the latest supported version of SQL Server, with Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher permitted only if approved by the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team.
All web applications must meet the State of Missouri's Accessibility Standard based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
All web applications must adhere to the W3 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance (WCAG 2.1 AA).
Vendor logos, branding or other company endorsements must not appear in web applications if there is a supported and licensed way to eliminate them from the display.
The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs by 4/25/2025, with MoDOT providing feedback for improvement.
The Offeror must demonstrate how the technology will create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties.
After adjustments to the tool, the Offeror must create a manual and provide training to ROW staff by 7/25/2025.
Once the system is developed and finalized, the Offeror must provide training to ROW staff, accompanied by a user manual for staff to reference.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025.
The final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary along with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study.
The final report must include a completed Technical Report Documentation page.
The Offeror must develop a final report detailing the tasks completed during the project, including all findings generated during the project's duration.
The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions.
The Offeror must provide a fee proposal to MHTC on the PRICE PAGE in accordance with the terms of the RFP.
The Offeror agrees to provide the services at the fees quoted under the terms of the RFP.
The Offeror must consult MHTC's representative regarding any concerns involved with the administration of the services provided under the RFP.
The Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate for all services defined in the Scope of Work on Section (4), Price Page, completed, signed and returned with the proposal.

The Offeror must indicate on the Price Page all costs for providing the services, broken out by salaries, benefits, operating expense, facilities and administration (F&A) cost, and miscellaneous expenses, with a total.
No material or reports prepared by the Offeror may be released to the public without the prior consent of MHTC's representative.
The Offeror may not assign or delegate any interest in, or transfer any interest in, the services to be provided without the prior written consent of MHTC's representative.

The Offeror must include the provisions of Section (3), paragraph I of the Agreement in every subcontract and take such action with respect to any subcontract as the Commission may direct to enforce those provisions.

The Offeror must, by sworn affidavit and documentation, affirm its enrollment and participation in a federal work authorization program such as E-Verify for employees working in connection with the contracted services, providing a completed copy of the E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding.
The Offeror must, by sworn affidavit, affirm that it does not knowingly employ any unauthorized alien in connection with the contracted services, using the affidavit provided as Exhibit A.

If the business entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership, each sole proprietor and each general partner must provide affirmative proof of lawful presence in the United States using the affidavit provided as Exhibit B.
All documents, reports and exhibits produced by the Offeror at the direction of MHTC's representative, and information supplied by MHTC's representative, remain the property of MHTC.

The Offeror must not disclose confidential factual matters provided to it to third parties except as required by statute, ordinance or court order or as authorized by MHTC's representative, and must notify MHTC immediately of any request for such information.

The Offeror must maintain all working papers and records relating to the Agreement and make them available at no charge to MHTC and/or the Missouri State Auditor during the term and for three (3) years from the date of final payment.
The Offeror may be asked prior to contract signing to provide certificates of insurance for general liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence.
The Offeror may be asked prior to contract signing to provide certificates of insurance for automobile liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence.
The Offeror may be asked prior to contract signing to provide a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent in accordance with state law.

items.text: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) is the issuing body, and the study is performed for MHTC and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts.

The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and MoDOT's Research Director Jen Harper is MHTC's designated representative for administering the agreement.

MoDOT must describe realty rights it acquires or conveys by metes and bounds unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.

Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, and a professional land surveyor must review each description before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the research.
The business driver is to determine whether AI and Machine Learning can produce a "first draft" legal land description from MHTC parameters that MoDOT Right of Way staff could then review and edit.

MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA each quarter.
The client wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," that determines the usefulness of AI/ML for drafting legal land descriptions.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.

The scope comprises six tasks: project management, literature review, providing a program to develop LLDs plus a proof of concept, training and user manual, draft report and research summary, and final report, research summary and presentation.

The Offeror must demonstrate on a variety of properties how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback (milestone 4/25/2025).
The Offeror must train Right of Way staff on the tool and supply a user manual, with the manual and training delivered 7/25/2025 after tool adjustments.
Deliverables include a draft final report, summary report and user manual due 11/3/2025, and a final report, summary report, presentation and user manual due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must conduct a literature review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
An interim presentation is required near the project mid-point (9/15/2025) to update MoDOT on progress and direction.
Proposals are due by email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov at 10 a.m. Central on August 21, 2024, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.
All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 4 p.m. Central on 7/17/2024, and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions publicly on 7/31/2024 and notifies submitters about project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.

The award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, evaluated after a responsiveness determination against criteria set by the Technical Advisory Committee, whose specific criteria and weights are not stated in the RFP.

The Work Plan must be narrative style, no more than ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, and must cover all items in Section 2 while recognizing MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

The proposal must be one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal (work plan and schedule), personnel, organization's project experience, team member experience, and organization's client references.

The proposal must identify experience in offering the requested services during the past three years and list at least three client officials (name, title, telephone) from the past three years as references.
The Offeror must submit a signed cost estimate on the Section (4) Price Page covering salaries, benefits, operating expense, F&A cost and miscellaneous, with a detailed budget developed later.
Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.
Before Task 3c proof-of-concept work begins, the Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs and obtain approval from MoDOT Information Systems.

Applications must use approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or supported .NET Framework 4.8+), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, and only C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the BRPT approves larger use.
No third-party tools or software may be used that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the BRPT and IS management.
Applications must be web-based, require no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), and meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard.
On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server, and no PII may be stored in any database table without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and records must be kept available for three years after final payment with no royalty or fee for MHTC's use.
The Data Management Plan is due within two weeks of the kick-off meeting (12/4/2024) and must describe how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30 and quarterly project updates feed the SPR Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA each quarter.
The contract is estimated to start November 1, 2024 and end 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named program before Task 3c proof-of-concept work may begin.
MoDOT must describe realty rights by metes and bounds unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
A professional land surveyor must review each description before a deed or similar document is presented to the grantor.
MoDOT's Research Director Jen Harper is MHTC's designated representative for administering the agreement.
The $175,000 not-to-exceed amount is treated as an all-inclusive ceiling covering every Price Page category, including F&A and miscellaneous, so the fee proposal is built to that total.

The program named for MoDOT Information Systems approval is assumed to be reviewable within roughly four to six weeks of submission, so the program is named at kick-off to protect the 4/25/2025 demonstration date.
The proof of concept is priced on a working sample of roughly ten to fifteen properties spanning full takes, partial takes and entirety conveyances, with MoDOT supplying the parcels and deed records.

Training is assumed to reach a ROW audience of up to about twenty staff, delivered as two remote instructor-led sessions plus recordings and the manual, with in-person delivery at MoDOT offices available within the ceiling if MoDOT prefers it.

The Standard Research Agreement, EPG Section 236.4.6.2, the Publication Guidelines and the Price Page cost estimate template are assumed to be the versions currently posted on the MoDOT website, and the Offeror will conform deliverables to them once obtained.

The LLD drafting program is assumed to be deployable in a MoDOT-approved environment with no licensing cost to MoDOT, using only the approved .NET stack and open-source components already cleared by the Best Practices Review Team.

Program approval gate before the proof of concept. The proposed solution names the LLD program at kick-off and assumes MoDOT Information Systems will approve it in four to six weeks, but the RFP sets no approval criteria, no review timeline and no route if approval is refused. If approval slips or is denied, the 4/25/2025 demonstration date and the whole downstream chain (training 7/25/2025, interim presentation 9/15/2025, draft deliverables 11/3/2025) move with it, and the bidder absorbs the rework inside a fixed ceiling. The approval is a hard precondition to Task 3c and the RFP leaves its duration and criteria unstated, so the four-to-six-week assumption is the bidder's own; a denial would force a rebuild of the program on a different stack.

Fixed $175,000 ceiling against an open-ended build and research scope. The solution commits to a full literature review, a working .NET web application, a proof of concept on real parcels, training, a manual and four report deliverables for a not-to-exceed $175,000, and treats that figure as all-inclusive of F&A and miscellaneous. If the build or the proof-of-concept revision cycle runs longer than planned, there is no headroom to recover the cost and the bidder funds the overrun. The RFP caps services at $175,000 and does not say whether the cap covers every Price Page category, so the all-inclusive reading is an assumption; a software build plus a research study on that budget leaves little contingency.

Proof-of-concept property count and variety undefined. The RFP requires a demonstration on a variety of properties but does not say how many parcels or which types, and the solution prices on an assumed ten to fifteen properties spanning full takes, partial takes and entirety conveyances with MoDOT supplying the deeds. If MoDOT expects a larger or harder sample, the surveyor review effort, the revision cycle and the training adjustments all grow without a matching budget line. The solution's own assumption sets the sample size, and the RFP leaves the number and types of parcels open, so the priced scope rests on a figure the client has not confirmed.

Exhibits A and B referenced but not supplied. The RFP requires a sworn affidavit that no unauthorized alien is employed using the affidavit provided as Exhibit A, and lawful-presence affidavits on Exhibit B for sole proprietorships or partnerships, but neither exhibit's content is in the document. The bidder cannot complete or sign the required affidavits from the RFP alone, and a missing or wrongly worded affidavit can make the proposal non-responsive. Both exhibits are listed as referenced documents not present in the PDF, and the affidavits are mandatory submission items tied to responsiveness.

Training audience size and delivery mode not specified. The solution assumes up to about twenty ROW staff reached through two remote instructor-led sessions plus recordings, with in-person delivery available within the ceiling if MoDOT prefers. If the audience is larger, spread across districts, or requires on-site sessions, the training and manual effort grows and the 7/25/2025 date tightens. The RFP fixes the training date but not the audience size, format or location, and the solution's twenty-staff, two-session model is an inference rather than a stated requirement.

Unreadable pages 19 and 20 may hide scope or pricing terms. Pages 19 and 20 carry only about nineteen words each and are more than half covered by an image, so their content could not be read. If those pages hold task detail, deliverable specifications or pricing instructions, the solution may be scoped or priced against an incomplete reading of the RFP. Two pages of the RFP are effectively unreadable, and they fall in the section that carries the task descriptions the solution is built on.

Standard Research Agreement not available before pricing. The contract will be governed by the Standard Research Agreement, which the RFP points to on the MoDOT website but does not include. Terms in it — indemnity, insurance limits, publication rights, payment timing — could add cost or risk the bidder has not priced, and the solution assumes the currently posted version will apply. The agreement is a referenced document absent from the RFP, and the solution's assumption that the posted version governs is unverified.

EPG Section 236.4.6.2 not provided, so description quality is unverifiable. The descriptions the program drafts must meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2, but that section is not in the RFP. The solution assumes the posted version and that the program can be built to it, so the acceptance criteria for the proof of concept and the surveyor review step rest on a document the bidder has not read. The EPG section is the substantive standard for the deliverable and is a referenced document missing from the RFP; the solution's conformance assumption is unverified.

Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses. The solution builds the LLD program on .NET with Python limited to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Best Practices Review Team approves more. If the AI/ML work needs Python for model training or inference, the bidder must either obtain BRPT approval or re-implement in C#, which changes the design and the effort. The RFP restricts Python use and the solution assumes open-source components are already cleared, but AI/ML tooling commonly depends on Python, so the assumption may not hold.

Accessibility conformance on a new web application. The program must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard, and the solution commits to both without an accessibility testing step in the schedule. Remediation discovered late, after the proof of concept or during training preparation, would force rework on a fixed budget and could delay the 7/25/2025 manual and training date. Accessibility is a mandatory technical requirement for a newly built application, and the solution's components do not name an audit or remediation activity.

PII in parcel and deed data without prior IS approval. The proof of concept works on real properties and deed records, which may contain personal identifying information, while the RFP forbids storing PII in any database table without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval. Discovering PII after the data is loaded would force a redesign of the data model and delay the Data Management Plan and the demonstration. The solution's Data Management Plan states no PII is stored without approval, but the RFP does not say whether the supplied deed records contain PII, so the risk turns on facts the RFP leaves open.

Publication Guidelines and summary template not supplied. The draft and final reports and the research summary must follow MoDOT's Publication Guidelines and research summary template, which are referenced on the website but not included. Format rework late in the schedule, when the 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 dates are close together, would compress the close-out and risk the final invoice date. The guidelines are a referenced document absent from the RFP, but the impact is formatting rework rather than a design change, and the solution already plans to conform once obtained.
